antidotes.why: Enthusiasm answers despair because Lakshmana and Hanuman set the will to go on against despair inside scenes of real loss.
Lift the self by the self so it does not sink into despair.
Faith assures that good deeds and effort are never lost or wasted.
Even at the lowest, do not let go of good company; find a friend who knows your kind of trouble.
Krishna's own answer to the collapse; mortality-flagged, week 3 only.

chains.summary: Seeing his own people, Arjuna is overcome and his limbs fail. He drops the bow and sits down in grief. He cannot tell which course is better. Confused about what is right, he asks to be taught.
chains.title: Arjuna's collapse

verses.m: Arjuna said: Krishna, when I see my own people standing here, eager to fight, I am overcome with pity and sorrow.
verses.sa: अर्जुन उवाचकृपया परयाऽऽविष्टो विषीदन्निदमब्रवीत् । दृष्ट्वेमं स्वजनं कृष्ण युयुत्सुं समुपस्थितम् ॥

verses.m: My limbs give way, my mouth is parched, my body trembles and my hair stands on end.
verses.sa: सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति । वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते ॥

verses.m: Sanjaya said: Having spoken this on the battlefield, Arjuna sank down on the seat of the chariot, letting fall his bow and arrows, his mind overwhelmed by grief.
verses.sa: सञ्जय उवाचएवमुक्त्वाऽर्जुनः संख्ये रथोपस्थ उपाविशत् । विसृज्य सशरं चापं शोकसंविग्नमानसः ॥

chains.summary: Lakshmana tells a grieving Rama that enthusiasm is strong, there is no strength greater than it, and nothing is out of reach for one who has it. Hanuman thinks in Lanka that not losing heart is the root of fortune. Sugriva says that one who gives in to despair sinks like an overloaded boat.
chains.title: No strength greater than the will to go on

verses.m: Noble brother, enthusiasm is powerful; there is no strength greater than enthusiasm. For the person who has it, nothing in the world is out of reach.
verses.sa: उत्साहो बलवानार्य नास्त्युत्साहात् परं बलम्। सोत्साहस्य हि लोकेषु न किंचिदपि दुर्लभम्॥

verses.m: Not losing heart is the root of success; not losing heart is the highest happiness. I will search again, in the places I have not yet searched.
verses.sa: अनिर्वेदः श्रियो मूलमनिर्वेदः परं सुखम्। भूयस्तत्र विचेष्यामि न यत्र विचयः कृतः॥

verses.m: Those who keep working surely see the fruit of their work. But once you sink into deep despair, you cannot rise again.
verses.sa: अवश्यं कुर्वतां तस्य दृश्यते कर्मणः फलम्। परं निर्वेदमागम्य नहि नोन्मीलनं क्षमम्॥

depicts.r: Complete Works, Vol. 5, Epistles, First Series, CIII, p. 160
depicts.sa: Yet I am sure to bob up soon and am waiting for the next turn.
depicts.why: Shows things are all gloomy with me just now.

depicts.r: Complete Works, Vol. 8, Epistles, Fourth Series, CLVII, p. 494
depicts.sa: I have been living in mental hell. It is partially lifted now, and I hope for better days, better states.

depicts.m: Arjuna said: Krishna, when I see my own people standing here, eager to fight, I am overcome with pity and sorrow.
depicts.sa: अर्जुन उवाचकृपया परयाऽऽविष्टो विषीदन्निदमब्रवीत् । दृष्ट्वेमं स्वजनं कृष्ण युयुत्सुं समुपस्थितम् ॥
depicts.why: Speaks while sinking at the sight of his own people on the other side.

depicts.m: My limbs give way, my mouth is parched, my body trembles and my hair stands on end.
depicts.sa: सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति । वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते ॥
depicts.why: Shows the body gives way first: limbs, mouth, skin, grip.

depicts.m: Sanjaya said: Having spoken this on the battlefield, Arjuna sank down on the seat of the chariot, letting fall his bow and arrows, his mind overwhelmed by grief.
depicts.sa: सञ्जय उवाचएवमुक्त्वाऽर्जुनः संख्ये रथोपस्थ उपाविशत् । विसृज्य सशरं चापं शोकसंविग्नमानसः ॥
depicts.why: Shows him putting down what he does best and sitting.

depicts.m: He (Jatayu) could not bear the sun's heat and turned back; I, being proud, flew on towards the sun. My wings burned in its boundless blaze, and I fell to the earth with a terrible cry.
depicts.sa: तेज न सहि सक सो फिरि आवा। मैं अभिमानी रबि निअरावा॥ जरे पंख अति तेज अपारा। परेउँ भूमि करि घोर चिकारा ॥
depicts.why: Shows the fall and the terrible cry.

depicts.m: Give him my greeting, friend, and say: Lord, you lack nothing, but kindness to the helpless is your promise. Remember it, and take away my heavy trouble.
depicts.sa: कहेहु तात अस मोर प्रनामा। सब प्रकार प्रभु पूरनकामा॥ दीन दयाल बिरिदु संभारी। हरहु नाथ सम संकट भारी ॥
depicts.why: Shows her calling her trouble heavy and herself helpless.

depicts.m: In such a world, what use is the enjoyment of desires, when one who feeds on them is seen to return here again and again? Please lift me out. In this world I am like a frog in a dark well. Sir, you are my way, you are my way.
depicts.sa: सोऽहमित्येतद्विधेऽस्मिन्संसारे किं कामोपभोगैर्यैरेवाश्रितस्यासकृदिहावर्तनं दृश्यत इत्युद्धर्तुमर्हसीत्यन्धोदपानस्थो भेक इवाहमस्मिन्संसारे भगवंस्त्वं नो गतिस्त्वं नो गतिः ॥

gloss: The sinking of the whole person when the will gives out is called viṣāda, and the Gita's first chapter is named for it (Arjuna-viṣāda-yoga).

heals.m: On this path no effort is lost and no harm results. Even a little of this practice protects one from great fear.
heals.sa: नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते । स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात् ॥

heals.m: Raise yourself by your own self; do not let yourself sink. For the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self.
heals.sa: उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥

heals.m: Noble brother, enthusiasm is powerful; there is no strength greater than enthusiasm. For the person who has it, nothing in the world is out of reach.
heals.sa: उत्साहो बलवानार्य नास्त्युत्साहात् परं बलम्। सोत्साहस्य हि लोकेषु न किंचिदपि दुर्लभम्॥
heals.why: Shows answers collapsing with the one power still in his hands.

heals.m: Not losing heart is the root of success; not losing heart is the highest happiness. I will search again, in the places I have not yet searched.
heals.sa: अनिर्वेदः श्रियो मूलमनिर्वेदः परं सुखम्। भूयस्तत्र विचेष्यामि न यत्र विचयः कृतः॥
heals.why: He answers his own collapse with a principle and a next step.

heals.m: Even when people fall into the hardest straits and feel helpless, they should not let go of good company, not even a little.
heals.sa: अपि कष्टतरां प्राप्तैर्दशां विवशतां गतैः । मनागपि न संत्याज्या मानवैः साधुसंगतिः ॥
heals.why: At the lowest point one thing is asked stay near good people.

heals.m: An angry Creator may destroy the swan's delight of roaming its lotus pond, but he cannot take away its famous skill of separating milk from water.
heals.sa: अम्भोजिनीवनविहारविलासमेव हंसस्य हन्ति नितरां कुपितो विधाता । न त्वस्य दुग्धजलभेदविधौ प्रसिद्धां वैदग्ध्यकीर्तिमपहर्तुमसौ समर्थः ॥
heals.why: Shows something remains after the loss.

heals.m: In prosperity the heart of the great becomes soft as a lotus; in adversity, hard as a mass of mountain rock.
heals.sa: सम्पत्सु महतां चित्तं भवत्युत्पलकोमलम् । आपत्सु च महाशैलशिलासङ्घातकर्कशम् ॥

heals.m: A ball struck down by the hand flies right back up. As a rule, the misfortunes of those who live rightly do not last.
heals.sa: पातितोऽपि कराघातैरुत्पतत्येव कन्दुकः । प्रायेण साधुवृत्तनामस्थायिन्यो विपत्तयः ॥
heals.why: Shows the fall as the start of the rebound.

hero.m: Arjuna said: Krishna, when I see my own people standing here, eager to fight, I am overcome with pity and sorrow.
hero.sa: अर्जुन उवाचकृपया परयाऽऽविष्टो विषीदन्निदमब्रवीत् । दृष्ट्वेमं स्वजनं कृष्ण युयुत्सुं समुपस्थितम् ॥

modern: Collapse, despair, the will giving way

practices.m: Friend mind, what is the use of so much chatter? Friend mind, all this is mere speculation. I have told you the heart of it: you are reality itself, vast as the sky.
practices.sa: सखे मनः किं बहुजल्पितेन सखे मनः सर्वमिदं वितर्क्यम् । यत्सारभूतं कथितं मया ते त्वमेव तत्त्वं गगनोपमोऽसि ॥

practices.m: Learn it by bowing down, by questioning, and by service. Those who are wise and have seen the truth will teach you that knowledge.
practices.sa: तद्विद्धि प्रणिपातेन परिप्रश्नेन सेवया । उपदेक्ष्यन्ति ते ज्ञानं ज्ञानिनस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः ॥
practices.why: Shows humility before a teacher who has seen the truth.

practices.m: Raise yourself by your own self; do not let yourself sink. For the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self.
practices.sa: उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥

practices.m: Laziness is the great enemy that lives in a person's own body. There is no friend like effort; one who works does not sink.
practices.sa: आलस्यं हि मनुष्याणां शरीरस्थो महारिपुः । नास्त्युद्यमसमो बन्धुः कुर्वाणो नावसीदति ॥

practices.m: Provisions for the wilderness of life, medicine that cuts the bonds of the world, rescue from sorrow and grief: the two syllables 'Ha-ri'.
practices.why: Trust is cultivated in two syllables.

practices.m: If an undertaking fails, do not torment yourself over it. Keep applying yourself again and again; this is the highest rule for those who lead.
practices.sa: विपन्ने च समारम्भे सन्तापं मा स्म वै कृथाः / घटेतैवं सदाऽऽत्मानं राज्ञामेष परो नयः
practices.why: Shows renewed exertion is called the supreme rule.

practices.m: Madhava is the father and the mother of all beings. Go to him for refuge, best of the Kurus; he is the refuge.
practices.sa: सर्वेषामेव भूतानां पिता माता च माधवः / गच्छध्वमेनं शरणं शरण्यं कौरवर्षभाः
practices.why: Shows he is parent to all.

practices.m: Even sinners who remember his name cross the boundless ocean of the world. You are his messengers: give up your timidity, keep Ram in your heart and find a way.
practices.sa: पापिउ जाकर नाम सुमिरहीं। अति अपार भवसागर तरहीं॥ तासु दूत तुम्ह तजि कदराई राम हृदयँ धरि करहु उपाई ॥
practices.why: Shows getting up and devising the means.

stories.l: Compulsions can take everything. Loyalty and patience can still bring you home.
stories.s: King Nala, possessed by the spirit Kali, gambles away his kingdom to his brother and abandons Damayanti in the forest. Years of separation and disguise follow, until Nala masters the dice and the two are reunited.

stories.l: Desire grows from what we imagine. Stop feeding it, and it fades.
stories.s: Manki spends all he has on a pair of oxen; both are killed in an accident. In his despair he sees through desire: it is born of his own imagining, and he resolves to forgive insults and stop feeding it. Bhishma adds Janaka's verse on owning nothing.
stories.t: Manki's song: desire, I know your root

stories.l: The hardest battle is with your own mind, and no one else can fight it for you.
stories.s: As Yudhishthira still grieves, Krishna tells him his real battle has begun: one fought alone, with his own mind, where 'mine' is death and 'not mine' is freedom.

stories.l: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.
stories.s: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
